frequency_question: How often do central banking/regulatory principals with the statutory power to activate a countercyclical capital buffer actually raise it above zero within any given 4-year economic cycle window?
membership_rule: Members are major jurisdictions (e.g., Federal Reserve, Bank of England, European Central Bank banking supervision, Reserve Bank of New Zealand) that established a framework for a countercyclical capital buffer post-2010 and operated it through at least one major credit cycle.

cases.name: Bank of England Financial Policy Committee CCyB activation
Reserve Bank of New Zealand CCyB activation
Swiss National Bank / FINMA CCyB activation
U.S. Federal Reserve Board CCyB consideration window
Federal Reserve Board CCyB post-pandemic window

coverage_note: 6 named cases drawn from major international banking regulators with comparable macro-prudential mandates.
known_gaps: Excludes smaller European national discretion implementations where data on active desire versus passive maintenance is ambiguous.
skeleton: Named jurisdictions with active CCyB frameworks evaluated over rolling 4-year windows where banking sector capital has been robust.
multiplier: 4 jurisdictions actively utilizing or maintaining the tool across multiple 4-year blocks yields roughly 10 distinct institutional evaluation periods.
validity_reason: The institutional architecture and domestic governance models of major central bank regulatory committees remain stable across this timeframe.
